title: Accounts Assistant
description:
We are recruiting for an Accounts Assistant to join a finance team. This is a varied role supporting the day-to-day financial operations, ensuring accurate financial records, efficient payment processing and effective budget monitoring.

Key Responsibilities
- Process supplier invoices, purchase orders and payments.
- Manage purchase and sales ledger activities.
- Raise invoices and monitor outstanding payments.
- Reconcile bank accounts and online payment systems.
- Investigate financial discrepancies and resolve supplier queries.
- Assist with budget preparation, monitoring and financial reporting.
- Monitor expenditure and highlight potential overspending.
- Obtain quotations and maintain purchasing records.
- Submit VAT returns and support internal and external audits.
- Maintain accurate financial records and ensure compliance with financial procedures and regulations.
- Handle confidential financial information professionally.

Skills and Experience
- Previous experience in an accounts or finance administration role.
- Knowledge of purchase ledger, sales ledger and bank reconciliations.
- Strong numerical skills and attention to detail.
- Excellent organisational and communication skills.
- Confident using accounting software, ideally QuickBooks.
- Ability to work independently, manage priorities and maintain confidentiality.

This role would suit an organised and proactive finance professional looking for a varied accounts position.

title: Bookkeeper

title: Credit Control/Sales Ledger
company: Gill Cooke Personnel Ltd T/A The Recruitment Group - Agency - Permanent
advertiser_name: Gill Cooke Personnel Ltd T/A The Recruitment Group
description:
We are recruiting for an experienced Sales Ledger / Credit Controller to join a busy and established finance team,

Hours can be either Full time 830am-5pm or Part Time 9am-3pm but you must be able to work Monday to Friday.
This role is based 4 days per week in the office near Burford and 1 day per week in the Chipping Campden office

This is a great opportunity for a confident and proactive finance professional with at least 3 years' experience in credit control or accounts receivable. You will play an important role in maintaining accurate customer accounts, supporting cash flow and ensuring outstanding debts are managed effectively.

Working as part of the wider finance team, you will take ownership of customer account administration, invoice processing, cash allocation and debt collection, helping to minimise aged debt and maintain strong customer relationships.

Key Responsibilities
Setting up new customer accounts, including carrying out Experian credit checks.
Managing the sales ledger and maintaining accurate customer account records.
Raising and processing credit notes through MS Automate reporting.
Inputting and allocating sales receipts at Group level.
Proactively chasing outstanding and aged debt, with a focus on reducing overdue balances.
Processing both EDI and non-EDI invoices (SEDI/SS).
Producing and distributing monthly customer statements.
Investigating and resolving customer account queries and payment discrepancies.
Supporting rebate calculations and reporting, including turnover and buying group sales input.
Working towards agreed credit control targets and supporting improvements in cash collection.

About You
To be successful in this role, you will ideally have:
A minimum of 3 years' experience in credit control, sales ledger or accounts receivable.
Experience managing customer accounts and chasing outstanding payments.
A good understanding of credit control procedures, credit terms and debt collection.
Experience with cash allocation, payment reconciliations and aged debt reporting.
Strong Excel skills and confidence using finance systems.
Excellent communication and negotiation skills, with the confidence to deal with customers at all levels.
Strong attention to detail and a methodical approach to your work.
The ability to prioritise workloads, meet deadlines and work towards targets.
A proactive approach to problem-solving and building positive customer relationships.

Desirable:
Experience working with B2 B or trade customers.
Previous experience within manufacturing or the construction sector.
AAT qualification or another relevant finance qualification.

If you have solid credit control experience, enjoy building customer relationships and are confident managing outstanding debt, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply today to find out more!

If you would like to know how we will store and process your data, please visit The Recruitment Group's home page to read our GDPR Data Protection information

title: Credit Controller
description:
The Credit Control Team look after all aspects of Debt Collections for our live & terminated customers. The team are responsible for collecting any missed payments and customer debt, resolving any customer issues regarding their Billing Account and when necessary, liaise with other departments to provide good customer care.

You will play a key role in ensuring that we minimize customer debt and reduce any bad debt. You will communicate regularly with our customers by telephone, email and in writing, responding to their queries in accordance with our Terms & Conditions, both for business and residential customers.

Note: this is a hybid role with 3 days per week based in our Abingdon Head Office. Please only apply if you are comfortable with this work pattern or are relocating to the area (please do mention in CV if that is the case).

Key Accountability & Responsibilities

Proactively follow up on overdue accounts via telephone and email.

Process card payments.

Maintain accurate records of communication.

Request write offs and refunds as required.

Promote direct debit sign-ups.

Agree and maintain payment plans and promises to pay.

Meet and exceed collection targets and performance KPIs.

Liaising with external debt collection agency where necessary.

Suspension of service for non-paying customers.

Liaise with key business stake holders to resolve any issues and customer queries in a timely and effective manner.

Knowledge & Skills

Previous experience in a credit control or accounts receivable role.

Strong communication skills, both verbal and written.

Ability to manage a high volume of accounts with precision and accuracy.

Proficient Excel ability (Basic to intermediate level)

Logical, numerate, detailed and analytical

Excellent time management, telephone manners and communication skills

A pro-active and customer focussed attitude.

Gigaclear is a growing Fibre Broadband (FTTP / FTTH) company, developing our fibre-to-the-premises broadband infrastructure to some of the most difficult to reach areas of the UK, empowering those communities with broadband to rival any city.

Staff rewards, benefits and opportunities

We foster a collaborative, engaging culture that empowers staff to grow and maximise their skills. We want to challenge our people in a fair environment where hard work is rewarded and a path for progression is open to all.
- Generous employer pension; up to 8% matched contribution
- Income protection & life assurance
- 25 days holiday (plus bank holidays), holiday purchase scheme and Yay Days!
- Health cash plan, 24/7 remote GP access and Employee Assistance Programme including counselling & legal advice
- Unlimited access to online training and development content via our Learning Management System
- Long service benefits and monthly employee recognition
- Enhanced maternity and paternity provisions
- Flexible working environment
- Health & Wellbeing initiatives and company funded social events

Our approach is to work guided by our mission, vision and values.

Our Mission - Empowering communities with brilliant broadband

Our Vision - Connected Communities

Our Values - Own it, Find the Right Way, Work Together, Win Together

title: Finance Administrator
description:

To support the Finance team the company are looking for a reliable and versatile Finance Administrator, to undertake a broad range of tasks spanning the functions of finance and accountancy

Based in an office in Sonning, near Reading, this person will be supporting the Finance Manager in a broad range of tasks including, but not limited to, the following:,
- Input all Sales and business costs via Sage and Construct.
- Invoice processing
- Respond to internal/external queries regarding supplier payments.
- Assisting with Creditor and debtor account controls
- Assisting with payroll, including PAYE records.

title: Graduate Finance Assistant
description:
Morgan McKinley Northern Home Counties are proud to be representing a manufacturing business based in Oxfordshire, who are looking to recruit a Graduate Finance Assistant to join their finance team.

This is an excellent opportunity for a recent graduate with a degree in Accounting and Finance (minimum 2:1) who is looking to take their first step into a career in finance.

Working as part of the existing finance team, you will gain exposure to a broad range of financial activities, develop your technical skills and build a strong foundation for a long-term career in finance.

No significant previous experience is required. We're looking for someone with a positive attitude, a willingness to learn and a genuine interest in developing within the finance profession.

Key responsibilities
- Supporting the day-to-day activities of the finance department.
- Assisting with accounts payable and accounts receivable processes.
- Processing invoices, expenses and financial transactions.
- Assisting with bank and balance sheet reconciliations.
- Supporting month-end reporting and financial close activities.
- Helping prepare financial reports, spreadsheets and analysis.
- Maintaining accurate financial records.
- Assisting with budgeting, forecasting and reporting where required.
- Working closely with colleagues across the wider business to resolve finance queries.

About you
- A degree in Accounting and Finance, Finance or a related discipline, achieving a minimum 2:1.
- Recently graduated from university
- A good understanding of basic accounting and financial principles.
- Strong numerical and analytical skills.
- Excellent attention to detail.
- Good IT skills, particularly Microsoft Excel.
- Strong communication and organisational skills.
- A proactive attitude and willingness to learn.

Working arrangements
- Location: Oxfordshire.
- Four days per week in the office.
- One day per week working from home.

title: HR and Payroll Officer
company: Not For Profit People - Agency - Permanent
description:
HR and Payroll Officer

Are you an organised and people-focused HR professional with payroll experience who enjoys delivering excellent service and building strong working relationships?

We are seeking an enthusiastic HR and Payroll Officer to join the Human Resources team in this full-time, permanent role.

This role offers the opportunity to work across the full employee lifecycle while building expertise in both HR and payroll. It is ideal for someone who enjoys balancing attention to detail with relationship-building and who takes pride in delivering a high-quality service.

Position: HR & Payroll Officer

Location: Kidlington, Oxford/hybrid

Hours: Full-time, 37 hours per week

Salary: £37,751.95 - £40,655.94 per annum

Contract: Permanent

Closing Date: Midnight on Tuesday 18 November 2026. Interviews will take place at Church House, Oxford: Friday 27 November 2026

The Role

You will join the Human Resources team, playing a key role in supporting employees, clergy, managers and senior leaders across the Diocese. This is an exciting opportunity to contribute to meaningful work, ensuring people are supported through efficient payroll, recruitment, learning and development, and employee lifecycle processes.

This is a varied and rewarding role within a professional and collaborative HR team that supports both the Diocesan Board of Finance and Diocesan Board of Education. You will provide reliable, confidential and people-centred HR and payroll support that helps employees, clergy and leaders do their best work.

You will also play a key role in delivering recruitment and onboarding activities, be the first point of contact for payroll-related matters and will help maintain robust controls and ensure compliance with statutory and organisational requirements.

About You

We are looking for an experienced HR and payroll professional who is highly organised, accurate and customer-focused, with a passion for providing excellent support and advice. You will be comfortable managing multiple priorities, handling sensitive information with discretion and working collaboratively with a wide range of stakeholders.

You will bring experience of HR administration and payroll processing within a busy organisational environment, together with strong communication skills and a proactive approach to problem-solving.

You will also have:
- Sound knowledge of generalist HR practices and payroll administration.
- Up-to-date knowledge of UK employment legislation and HMRC requirements relating to payroll, tax and statutory payments.
- Experience supporting recruitment, onboarding, learning and development, employee relations and performance management activities.
- Strong IT skills, including Microsoft Office applications, and experience using HR management systems and payroll systems.
- High levels of accuracy and attention to detail, particularly when working with payroll and employee data and maintaining accurate employee records.
- Excellent organisational skills with the ability to manage competing priorities and meet deadlines.

A CIPD and/or CIPP qualification or membership would be advantageous, although applications are welcomed from candidates with transferable skills and experience.

You do not need to be a practising Christian to work here. Around half of staff are not practising Christians, but all are comfortable working within the Christian ethos and values that underpin the organisation's work.

The successful candidate must have the right to live and work in the United Kingdom. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for interviews. We are particularly keen to receive applications from UK Minority Ethnic / Global Majority heritage and disabled candidates, who are currently underrepresented.

You may have experience in other areas such as HR, Human Resources, Personnel, People, HR Officer, Human Resources Officer, Personnel Officer, People Officer, Payroll, Payroll Officer, Payroll Assistant, HR Assistant, Finance Officer, Finance Assistant, HR and Finance, HR and Payroll.

Please note this role is advertised by the recruitment agency acting for the client, Not For Profit People.

title: Payroll Administrator
description:
Competitive Salary Flexible & Hybrid Working Excellent Benefits

We are currently recruiting for an experienced Payroll Administrator to join a well-established and forward-thinking professional services firm for a fixed 12 month contract.

This is an excellent opportunity to join a supportive team and take responsibility for delivering a high-quality payroll service to a varied portfolio of clients. The role offers a good level of autonomy, a varied workload and the opportunity to work within a business that continues to invest in its payroll and HR services.

You will be responsible for processing a portfolio of weekly and monthly client payrolls, ensuring accuracy, compliance and timely delivery. Working closely with colleagues and clients, you will play an important part in maintaining the smooth running of the payroll function throughout the period of cover.

Tasks include:

Client Payroll
- Processing weekly and monthly client payrolls from start to finish, including data input, calculations, payslips, RTI submissions and client reporting.
- Managing pension administration for allocated clients, including auto-enrolment.
- Preparing and submitting monthly CIS returns within HMRC deadlines.
- Preparing BACS payment files for employee net pay and HMRC liabilities.
- Dealing with client payroll queries promptly and professionally, escalating more complex matters where appropriate.
- Maintaining clear communication with clients regarding deadlines and outstanding information.

Internal Payroll & Administration
- Processing the firm's monthly payroll, subject to final Partner review.
- Following established payroll procedures and keeping documentation accurate and up to date.
- Providing basic payroll administration cover for colleagues when required.
- Completing structured handovers at the beginning and end of the assignment.

The person:

The successful candidate will be an experienced payroll professional with a methodical approach, excellent attention to detail and the ability to manage deadlines confidently.

You will ideally have:
- Previous experience processing weekly and monthly payrolls, preferably from start to finish.
- A good understanding of HMRC payroll requirements and RTI submissions.
- Experience of pension administration and auto-enrolment.
- Knowledge of CIS payroll processes.
- Strong organisational and communication skills.
- The ability to manage your own workload while providing excellent client service.

Our client offers

The firm offers an attractive benefits package, including:
- Competitive salary, dependent on experience.
- Flexible and hybrid working, including flexitime and working from home.
- Early finish every Friday, with the office closing at 2.30pm.
- Study support, where relevant.
- Pension scheme.
- 23 days' annual leave, plus bank holidays.
- Access to a corporate reward scheme.
- Quarterly social events.
- Free on-site parking.

If you are an experienced Payroll Administrator looking for your next opportunity within a professional and supportive environment, we would love to hear from you.

If you are an accurate, client-focused payroll professional looking for your next 12 month role, we would love to hear from you. Apply now!
